messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU pool 'gpus-prod-eu' queue depth spiked to 5.3x baseline at 2026-03-15T01:17:56Z. Autoscaler attempted scale but observed driver/node crashes during provisioning. Affected routes: /v1/generate (high qps). Potential customer impact: increased latency and throttling. Paging on-call.

Maya (oncall-sre): I'm on it. seeing steady queue growth on the ingestion side. Can someone pull node crash logs and recent deploys? @Evan @Priya

Evan (runtime-eng): pulling runtime logs now. early signs: repeated CUDA Xid 4 and Xid 13 entries followed by driver restarts. looks like a driver rollout from yesterday had a kernel module change.

Priya (infra): Confirming — cloud autoscaler shows repeated scale-up attempts hitting maxPodCreationFailures. Cloud provider reports kernel oops on new nodes during gpu-driver-install step.

Jon (support): Heads-up: two customers (acct-329, acct-118) reported 5xxs and long tail latency. Marking P2 for customer-impacted endpoints. Zoe, can you draft a short customer message if impact confirmed?

Zoe (cs): will prep a short note once we confirm scope. prefer holding until we have mitigation steps.

Maya (oncall-sre): Quick mitigation plan proposals: 1) Pause autoscaler/increase failure threshold 2) Cordon new nodes so we don't schedule until safe 3) Revert driver rollout to previous driver package 4) Apply temporary rate-limiting to non-critical tenants. Which ones can we throttle without breaking SLAs? @Jon

Jon (support): We can throttle free-tier and burst customers first. Leave reserved/dedicated customers alone. I'll coordinate lists.

Evan (runtime-eng): Revert is my preference. I'm seeing this in logs:

```
[2026-03-15T01:15:03Z] nvidia: kernel: GPU 0: Xid 4: GPF during copy engine
[2026-03-15T01:15:04Z] kubelet: container runtime: crashloop backoff, reason: signal 6
[2026-03-15T01:15:07Z] driver-installer: ERR: unresolved symbol, module taint
```

Evan (runtime-eng): If we revert the driver package to v470.63 which was stable, we should stop new nodes from OOMing/crashing. I'll prepare a rollback and a safe patch.

Priya (infra): Meanwhile I'll bump the autoscaler to allow higher max nodes + increase the create failure threshold to avoid rapid oscillation. But that might spin up more nodes which could also crash. So first step should be rollback.

Maya (oncall-sre): Agreed. Evan, do you have the rollback command? deploy-bot, can you run a controlled rollback to driver v470.63 in eu-prod pool? We need a canary of 2 nodes first.

deploy-bot: Received rollback job: drivers/rollback v470.63 -> targeting pool gpus-prod-eu. Canary size 2. ETA ~ 4m. Will post status.

ops-bot: Note: Autoscaler temporarily paused for pool gpus-prod-eu by Priya at 2026-03-15T01:19:12Z.

Evan (runtime-eng): Canary pods coming up. Monitoring nvidia-smi and dmesg. Example to check on nodes:

```
ssh gpu-canary-01
sudo systemctl status nvidia-driver
sudo dmesg | tail -n 50
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,memory.used --format=csv
```

Maya (oncall-sre): I'm seeing canary nodes stabilizing. No Xid errors on canary after rollback so far. Good sign. Can we gradually replace crashed nodes once rollback completes?

Priya (infra): Yes. Plan: 1) finish driver rollback, 2) uncordon canary and drain+replace failed nodes one by one, 3) re-enable autoscaler with conservative thresholds. I'll run drains with 30m grace.

Evan (runtime-eng): I'll watch for regressions. If Xid returns, we'll immediately quiesce pool and failover routing. Also adding extra logging for dmesg+driver installs to capture root cause.

Jon (support): Sending holding message to customers impacted with short note: "We're investigating increased errors/latency affecting inference. We're rolling back a recent driver change; we'll update in 30 mins." :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Zoe (cs): sent to acct-329 and acct-118, copied on-prem contacts. Will escalate if SLA thresholds breached.

Maya (oncall-sre): Quick ask: do we have a runbook number for driver-rollbacks? I'm following SRE - GPU Runtime rollback v2. Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-driver-rollback

Evan (runtime-eng): Adding a waffle: root cause likely regression in kernel module dependency ordering. We'll open a ticket with vendor + add extra preflight checks to driver-installer.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback successful: drivers v470.63 applied to 2 canary nodes at 2026-03-15T01:22:48Z. No crash events observed in 3m.

Maya (oncall-sre): OK proceed with staged rollback. Priya, proceed with drain/replace on crashed nodes. Keep autoscaler paused until we have 20m of stability.

Priya (infra): Starting drain for gpu-node-23 -> cordon+drain. Command run:

```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-23
kubectl drain gpu-node-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
```

Priya (infra): Node drained, recreating with stable image. Will monitor node replace activity.

ops-bot: Observability: queue depth reduced from 5.3x to 1.7x after canary and initial node replacements. Latency tail improving.

Maya (oncall-sre): Good. Next: re-enable autoscaler in 20m with new thresholds: minNodes=8, maxNodes=40, createFailureThreshold=10. Priya to confirm.

Priya (infra): Confirmed and will apply after 20m quiet window.

Evan (runtime-eng): I'm also adding extra guard to the driver-installer that verifies module loads and runs a quick GPU smoke test before marking node ready. Patch posted to infra PR #4821.

Jon (support): Two customers report improvements. No longer seeing 5xxs. Keeping watch for edge cases.

Zoe (cs): Sent updated note to customers: "Root cause identified as driver regression; we reverted and are replacing affected nodes. Services recovering. Will follow up with RCA." :white_check_mark:

Maya (oncall-sre): Summary of actions taken:
- Rolled back GPU driver to v470.63 (Evan, deploy-bot)
- Paused autoscaler and canaried rollback (Priya, Maya)
- Drained and replaced crashed nodes (Priya)
- Rate-limited non-critical tenants temporarily (Jon)
- Added smoke-checks to installer (Evan)
- Customer comms sent (Zoe)

Maya (oncall-sre): I'll hand off to Priya for overnight stability monitoring. Priya, you're the primary owner for next 6h. If things look green after 60m, re-enable autoscaler. I'll update incident tracker with P1 -> P2 reduction and open RCA.

Priya (infra): Taking handoff. Monitoring dashboards and node health. Channel will stay open. ETA for autoscaler re-enable: 2026-03-15T02:40:00Z (if stable).

Evan (runtime-eng): I'll follow up on root-cause analysis and vendor report. Assigning myself to RCA ticket R-2026-331.

Maya (oncall-sre): Thanks team. Closing active paging. If anything flares, page oncall as usual. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident note appended to ticket INC-20260315-17. Next on-call: Priya (infra) 2026-03-15T01:30:00Z.
